title: A memory-information window in finite-duration quantum control
summary: Environmental noise is a major source of decoherence and errors in quantum systems. In a non-Markovian environment, the noise has a finite correlation time, and the system can retain information about its previous interactions with the environment. Here, we investigate how such environmental memory can be observed through a finite-duration coherent quantum operation. Coherent control dynamically reshapes the stochastic coupling operator and thereby changes how two-time noise correlations affect the quantum process.
